value.rationale: The 60-vertex uniform Archimedean solid is a canonical object, and exact complete distributions of vertex-supported simplex volumes, second-best gap, and multiplicities are natural invariants useful for optimizing discrete tetrahedra, symmetry-class testing and future polyhedral comparison. Unlike a re-reporting of the known maximum, the 381-level census resolves all nonmaximal levels and supplies a checkable independent moment identity.
residual_risks: No general theorem for an arbitrary Archimedean family is necessary for this finite exact natural classification.

final_claim: For 60 vertices of the unit-edge regular truncated icosahedron, all C(60,4)=487635 vertex tetrahedra realize exactly 381 distinct volumes (a+bφ)/48, with complete spectrum.tsv multiplicity table. Largest two levels are (100+164φ)/48 and (100+160φ)/48, each 120 tetrahedra and one congruence class; the vertex-supported gap is φ/12 and the squared-determinant sum equals 480000(10+9φ)^3.
limitations: Continuous inscribed tetrahedra have no positive next-best gap; claim strictly vertex-supported.
